RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 35

An all-male panel is not evidence of discrimination on its own. In many clinical fields the senior pool skews male, so the composition is as likely to reflect who was available as any bias. It's context, not a sign.

Your stronger points are concrete: a PhD plus eight years actually running a section versus a master's and a management course, and "broad leadership experience" stated without specifics. That's a documented qualifications gap. Also, two weeks of silence on a written request for reasons is itself a procedural problem.

So lead with the comparison and the unanswered request. Mention panel composition only if you later file a formal complaint, as background — never as your opening argument.
